title: A hello to nobody
step: Level 3, rung 6 — standing in the doorway
note:
Used three times. Collides with door-stay-03-conversation, and the difference is posture: this is STANDING SQUARE in the doorway for a quick hello; that one is leaning on the door, hip cocked, hand in a pocket, settled in for half a minute.

The continuity:room reference to door-cover.png was removed before the first restyle round. Every rung carried both it and the continuity:ladder reference to the rung before, and their instructions contradict each other on the one thing the ladder cannot get wrong: the ladder role says match the previous rung's camera exactly, and the room role says match door-cover's camera exactly — but door-cover is a different shot, with the door open and the guest in it. Two attachments arguing about the camera is the shape of the round-1 failure. The previous rung is the room reference, and a better one: the tan-era record shows the camera holding to four pixels across four generations when each frame was attached to the last and nothing else competed. door-stay-03-onestep keeps its door-cover reference because it is the head of the ladder and has no previous rung to use instead.

The camera clause was added after round 22 of door-stay-03-handle drifted: the floor line dropped 29px, the door top rose 10px and the door widened, while the three rungs before it had held the floor line to two pixels. The ladder attachment alone did not hold it. Stating the framing as proportions of the frame put it back to the pixel on the next round.
scene: Interior entry hall, side view, camera at standing eye level. This is the same room, the same camera position and the same distance from the viewer as the other rungs of this ladder: Lucy's rectangular cool-grey dog bed on the left, the closed charcoal front door on the right, and a clear span of taupe-grey floor between them, with the whole walk from bed to door visible in frame. Lucy lies on the bed in a settled down — elbows and hips on the bed, head up and level, watching calmly. Her size in frame, the bed's position and the camera never change between these pictures. No leash. THE CAMERA DOES NOT MOVE: keep the framing of the attached previous rung exactly. The line where the wall meets the floor runs straight across the picture at 62% of its height, so the wall fills the upper five-eighths and the floor the lower three-eighths. The door's top edge sits at 9.5% of the frame height and the door occupies from 75% to 93% of the frame width. Do not zoom in, do not lower the camera, and do not enlarge the door. Only one thing changes from the previous rung: the front door is now open wide enough to stand in, and the handler stands squarely in the doorway with her weight even on both feet, upright, facing out onto an empty porch and speaking to nobody — mouth slightly open mid-word, one hand lifted in a small brief wave. She is NOT leaning on the door, not resting a shoulder against the frame, and not slouching: she is standing straight, as if this will take five seconds. The porch beyond is empty — pale daylight and flat spruce foliage, no visitor, nobody there. Lucy holds her down on the bed.
mustBeTrue: the handler stands square and upright in the open doorway with her weight even on both feet, not leaning on the door or the frame, the porch beyond her is empty with nobody on it, and Lucy stays lying on her bed.
